title: External subprocess termination around composite-checkpoint issuance and recovery

preserved_failure_lineage.summary: The first external-SIGKILL harness duplicated the Pilot 8 issuance transition using private internals instead of executing DurableCompositeJournalAuthority.issue() itself. The duplicate path was materially non-identical, so its 14/14 green result was preserved but not accepted as exact-mechanism evidence.

The narrow correspondence repair left production checkpoint code unchanged. A test-only transparent SQLite connection proxy observed the exact SQL/commit boundaries while the child executed DurableCompositeJournalAuthority.issue() itself. No frozen endpoint, expected result, state transition, SQL predicate, authentication rule, recovery rule, generation rule, or authority boundary was relaxed.

supported_claim: On the tested same-host SQLite prototype running on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12, the exact DurableCompositeJournalAuthority.issue() path remained fail-closed and replay-safe across the preregistered parent-driven external SIGKILL boundaries. Killing before durable PENDING produced no false CURRENT; a committed unauthenticated PENDING remained non-current and unrecoverable; an authenticated PENDING remained non-current until exact matching recovery and then promoted exactly once; killing after the CURRENT UPDATE but before COMMIT rolled the promotion back to authenticated PENDING and allowed one exact later reconciliation; killing after CURRENT COMMIT but before response preserved the durable valid CURRENT checkpoint and exact retry returned the same issuance without duplication. State drift, semantic rebinding, and a competing same-generation issuance remained denied, and clean higher-generation issuance remained live. The parent verified the readiness marker PID matched the live child PID and that termination was external SIGKILL rather than cooperative worker cleanup.
not_proven: Kernel panic, VM reset, or whole-host disappearance semantics
Storage-controller, filesystem barrier, drive-cache, torn-page, bit-rot, or all SQLite WAL/checkpoint interleavings
Separate-process isolation or non-possession of the composite checkpoint authentication/signing key by the writer
Atomic commitment across independent storage systems
Atomic commitment to an external KMS, HSM, or checkpoint service
Exactly-once semantics for arbitrary remote side effects
Protection after compromise of both durable state and the checkpoint authentication key or trusted-minimum authority
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 10: isolate composite-checkpoint authentication/signing authority from the writer process. The writer must possess no checkpoint signing key and must request a narrowly bound signature/authorization from a distinct process that independently enforces scope, generation, predecessor, ledger digests, permit-authority epoch, issuance identity, replay/semantic-rebinding rules, and fail-closed behavior across signer restart or unavailability.
